liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help On The Way** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer says the Help, Slipknot and Fire sequence captures everything about the show; Reviewer calls the Help, Slip, Fire sequence perfect [4][23][29][30][33]
- **Bird Song** (1 review, 1 other source): Reviewer calls Bird Song a powerful first set closer; A whistler in Bird Song and an angry patron were removed from the matrix [11][28]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Reviewer says the keyboardist Vince sounds like a carnival organist during Fire [34]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer says Estimated Prophet deflates the energy built by the preceding sequence [33]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer says the Morning Dew is overshadowed by the Help, Slip, Fire sequence [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-09-20.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-5700.34799.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd91-09-20.sbd.ladner.21647.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 4.11/5 by 18 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer praises the full bass and a tight changeover in the recording; Reviewer says keyboards are mixed too high, exposing weak playing [29][34]
- **gd1991-09-20.AKG451.Currier.Keo.124201.Flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Some of Drums/Space is missing from this recording [4]
- **gd1991-09-20.153420.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 164 min [11]
- **gd91-09-20.aud.horwath-goetz.18596.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 18 songs; 136 min; rated 4.14/5 by 7 [20]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says a recent update makes this a great-sounding soundboard [33]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was overseas when news of Jerry's death arrived and had a tape of this show with them [23]
- Reviewer attended the Boston Garden run, had very good seats, and watched Jerry closely, who seemed in top form [24]
- Reviewer and a friend snuck onto the floor on night one and sat in empty seats beside the soundboard [27]
- Ticketing mix-up reportedly allowed them to return to the same spot for all six shows without being hassled [27]
- Reviewer was a taper at the show, having seen the band about 200 times [30]
- Reviewer describes the run as having had cool shows and some great weather [30]
- Local reviewer says the 1991 Garden shows far outshine the band's Garden shows of the next two years [28]
- Reviewer says the setlist looks better on paper than the show delivers [34]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-09-20.sbd.ladner.tetzeli.fix-5700.34799.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: Fix of shnid 5700 [1]. Also: Uploader made the CD 2 to CD 3 transition seamless, fixing sector boundaries verified with shntool and adding overlapping fade tracks [1]
- **gd91-09-20.sbd.ladner.21647.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Soundboard source is unknown; hosted by tol.etree.org and seeded via bittorrent by Tony G [2]
- **gd1991-09-20.AKG451.Currier.Keo.124201.Flac2496**: taped by Mr. Currier; transferred by Keo; source: Master Audience Recorded By Mr. Currier, Transfer By Keo; AKGC451/CK1's > AKG 9V Phantom Power Supply > Marantz PDM-430 > Dolby B, Tapes Maxell MX-s 100's;… [4]. Also: Audience recording made with AKG451 microphones by Currier and shared by him [4]
- **gd1991-09-20.153420.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: source: A photoLeon Matrix [11]. Also: Matrix by Joe Noel combines Dan O'Neill's front-of-board recording with a soundboard by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Soundboard was transferred and processed by Charlie Miller and speed corrected for the matrix [11]
- **gd91-09-20.aud.horwath-goetz.18596.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recorded with nakamichi 300 plus cp4 (shotguns) from OTS Mark Horvath [20]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Boston Garden - September 20, 1991](https://www.dead.net/show/september-20-1991) [36]
- Fan art by D.King Gallery: [Reonegro Grateful Dead 9/20/1991 Boston Backstage Pass](https://www.dking-gallery.com/store/Dead_Pass_910920.html) [37]

claims.text: Reviewer was overseas when news of Jerry's death arrived and had a tape of this show with them
Reviewer says the Help, Slipknot and Fire sequence captures everything about the show
Reviewer attended the Boston Garden run, had very good seats, and watched Jerry closely, who seemed in top form
Reviewer says the Morning Dew is overshadowed by the Help, Slip, Fire sequence
Reviewer and a friend snuck onto the floor on night one and sat in empty seats beside the soundboard
Ticketing mix-up reportedly allowed them to return to the same spot for all six shows without being hassled
Local reviewer says the 1991 Garden shows far outshine the band's Garden shows of the next two years
Reviewer calls Bird Song a powerful first set closer
Reviewer praises the full bass and a tight changeover in the recording
Reviewer calls the Help, Slip, Fire sequence perfect
Reviewer was a taper at the show, having seen the band about 200 times
Reviewer says opening the second set with Help, Slip, Franklin's was routine, but this night broke that pattern deliberately
Reviewer describes the run as having had cool shows and some great weather
Reviewer says a recent update makes this a great-sounding soundboard
Reviewer calls Help, Slip, Fire a special feature of the show
Reviewer says Estimated Prophet deflates the energy built by the preceding sequence
Reviewer says the setlist looks better on paper than the show delivers
Reviewer says keyboards are mixed too high, exposing weak playing
Reviewer says the keyboardist Vince sounds like a carnival organist during Fire
Uploader made the CD 2 to CD 3 transition seamless, fixing sector boundaries verified with shntool and adding overlapping fade tracks
Soundboard source is unknown; hosted by tol.etree.org and seeded via bittorrent by Tony G
Audience recording made with AKG451 microphones by Currier and shared by him
Some of Drums/Space is missing from this recording
Uploader recalls the unexpected Help, Slip, Fire transition sending the crowd wild, with everyone embracing
Matrix by Joe Noel combines Dan O'Neill's front-of-board recording with a soundboard by Don Pearson and Dan Healy
Soundboard was transferred and processed by Charlie Miller and speed corrected for the matrix
A whistler in Bird Song and an angry patron were removed from the matrix
